title: DIY vs. Professional Painting: When to Hire a Pro
description: DIY makes sense for a small room with simple walls. Hire a pro for high ceilings, exteriors, cabinets, big color changes, repairs, or when your time is worth more. Here's how to decide.
author: Chris Petkau
content:
Short answer: DIY painting makes sense for a small room with simple walls, a single color and a free weekend. Hire a professional for anything high, detailed or hard to redo: two-story walls and stairwells, exteriors, cabinets, big color changes, drywall repairs, or whole-home projects where time matters.

When DIY Painting Makes Sense

  • One room with standard 8-foot ceilings

  • Walls in good shape with only a few nail holes

  • Similar color to what's there now

  • You have the tools and the time for a full weekend per room

  • The result doesn't need to be perfect, for example a garage or storage room

When to Hire a Pro

  • Heights. Two-story foyers, stairwells and vaulted ceilings need scaffolding or tall ladders. Falls are the biggest DIY painting risk.

  • Exteriors. Siding, stucco, brick and trim need pressure washing, caulking, scraping, priming and the right products for Gulf Coast heat and humidity. See exterior painting.

  • Cabinets. Getting a smooth, durable finish takes degreasing, sanding, bonding primer and usually spraying. A failed DIY cabinet job costs more to fix than doing it right the first time.

  • Big color changes. Dark to light, or bold accent walls, need primer and extra coats to cover evenly.

  • Repairs. Cracks, water stains and damaged drywall need patching and texture matching before paint. See drywall repair.

  • Whole-home projects. A crew can finish in days what takes a homeowner weeks of weekends.

  • Selling soon. Buyers notice drips, uneven lines and patchy coverage.

Comparing the Real Costs

DIY saves labor, but count everything: brushes, rollers, trays, tape, drop cloths, ladders, caulk, patching compound, primer and quality paint, plus your time. Mistakes such as wrong products, skipped primer or poor prep often show up as peeling or uneven color months later. A professional quote includes materials, prep, cleanup and a workmanship warranty. What to Look For in a Painter

  • A written, detailed quote that spells out prep, products and number of coats

  • Proof of liability insurance

  • A written workmanship warranty

  • Recent reviews and photos of similar projects

Our guide to questions to ask a painting contractor covers the rest.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is it cheaper to paint a room yourself?

Usually, if you already own the tools and the walls are in good shape. The savings shrink quickly with high ceilings, repairs or color changes.

How long does it take a professional to paint a room?

Most single rooms take one to two days. See how long interior painting takes.

Can I do the prep and have a pro paint?

Sometimes, but most professionals prefer to do their own prep because it's what their warranty depends on.
